title: fix(types): declare record:related_list's top-level filter as the protocol's rule array (objectui#10199)
body:
Fixes #10199
Clause-②: yes

## What this does

This carries out the ruling on the card (comment `5814478513`, protocol first, maintainer 「同意」): `RecordRelatedListComponentProps.filter` in `packages/types/src/record-components.ts` goes from `any` to **`ViewFilterRule[]`**. That matches `@objectstack/spec`'s `RecordRelatedListProps.filter`, which is `z.array(ViewFilterRuleSchema)` ("Additional filter criteria for related records"). The consumer prop in `packages/plugin-detail/src/RelatedList.tsx` keeps `ViewFilterRule[] | FilterNode` and is not in this diff. The `FilterNode` half is the value `ElementDataSourceGate` composes at runtime, and nobody authors it.

- `packages/types/src/record-components.ts`: the one-line narrowing, with a doc block saying why this face carries the array while the consumer carries the union. `ViewFilterRule` was **already imported** here (objectui#9964 added it for `add.picker.filter`) and is already re-exported from the package index. No new export, no new import.
- `packages/types/src/__tests__/p1-spec-alignment.test.ts`: the one authoring fixture that wrote a non-array shape (`filter: [['active', '=', true]]`, an array of tuples) now writes the rule array `[{ field: 'active', operator: 'equals', value: true }]`, with the reason stated at the call site.
- `packages/types/src/__tests__/related-list-filter-rule-array-10199.test.ts`: the new pin (see below).
- `.changeset/10199-related-list-filter-rule-array.md`: `'@object-ui/types': minor`.

**Docs face: none in this diff.** No `content/docs/**` page authors a value on this key. The only `record:related_list` JSON example (`content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`) has no `filter`, and `content/docs/guide/data-source.md` describes the key only in prose. So `check:doc-examples` is not owed.

**Zod mirror: none.** `packages/types/src/zod/` has no schema for the record-component props, and no other mirror exists in the repo. None was added, because a new schema would be a new export. The plugin-detail registry input already declares this key as `type: 'array', of: 'object'`.

## Census: who writes this key, and whether it is authoring

The premise was re-measured on `origin/main` `8b1f0661` before any edit. Installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0, `dist/ui` has `filter: z.array(ViewFilterRuleSchema).optional().describe("Additional filter criteria for related records")`. The mirror said `filter?: any;` and `RelatedList` says `filter?: ViewFilterRule[] | FilterNode;`.

For the typed sites, the compiler did the census. After the narrowing, `@object-ui/types` `type-check` produced **exactly one** `TS2322`, at the p1-spec-alignment fixture. `@object-ui/plugin-detail` `type-check` (main and test tsconfigs) stayed green. It ran against a rebuilt `@object-ui/types` dist, and a reverse probe confirmed that dist was the one being read (see Verification).

| site | writes via | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `p1-spec-alignment.test.ts` ("should define RecordRelatedListComponentProps") | the authoring type | **corrected** from an array of tuples to the rule array |
| `detail-view-related-retired-7997.test.ts`, `detailRendererUndeclaredKeys-8649.test.ts` | the authoring type | no `filter` authored, unaffected |
| `record-related-list.tsx` (fenced) | its `schema` type is derived from this interface | not edited. Its only read, `filter={schema.filter}`, hands the value to `RelatedList`'s union and compiles |
| `RecordRelatedListRenderer.*.test.tsx` (fenced) | untyped record spreads (string keys, `any` values) | not edited. What they author on this key is already the rule array; `[['x', '=', 1]]` there is the binding's `dataSource.filter`, a different key |
| `ElementDataSourceGate` (`useElementDataSourceSchema`) | its own untyped schema copy (`base` cast to an untyped string-keyed record, returned `as S`) | **runtime write, not authoring.** Keeps compiling |
| `RecordDetailView` → `deriveRelatedLists` → `buildDefaultPageSchema` | untyped `componentNode` props | **runtime write, not authoring** (the FK's `relatedListFilter`, see Acceptance notes). Keeps compiling |
| `content/docs/**`, `examples/**`, `skills/**`, `packages/plugin-detail/README.md` | none | none author a non-array value on this key; the README's authoring prose already reads `[{ field, operator, value }]` |

## Pins

`related-list-filter-rule-array-10199.test.ts` follows `related-list-add-picker-filter-mirror-9964.test.ts`, the sibling repair on this interface.

- **Type-level legs** (compiled by `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): the mirror's `filter` is `Equal` to the spec's `z.input` of `RecordRelatedListProps['filter']` (derived, not restated) and to `ViewFilterRule[] | undefined`. An authored rule array and an empty `[]` compile. Two `@ts-expect-error` literals are refused: the composed AST node (`['and', ...]`) and the array of tuples. A third `@ts-expect-error` asserts the declaration is not `any`.
- **Diagnostic legs** (TS API under vitest, against the mirror SOURCE by relative path, so no dist sits between the edit and the reading): 11 cases. The canonical array is accepted. Six wrong shapes are refused: the composed AST, the array of tuples, a MongoDB-style record, an expression string, a bare rule object, and a rule missing `field`. A reader can no longer treat the value as a string. Three controls behave the same on both legs. Every case is compiled a second time against the pre-fix `any` declaration, and `EXPECTED_FLIPS` names the seven that flip.
- **Agreement with the protocol**: every authored value the compiler judges is also handed to the installed spec's own `RecordRelatedListProps.shape.filter.safeParse`, and the compiler's actual verdict must equal the parse's verdict on each one.

**Consumer control (the runtime hand-off).** `FilterNode` lives in `@object-ui/core` and `RelatedList` in `@object-ui/plugin-detail`, and neither is importable from zero-dependency `@object-ui/types`. The claim also keeps pins under `packages/types/src/__tests__/`. So the control is the existing consumer-side suites, run against this branch:
- `RelatedList.listFilter.test.tsx` "accepts the AST node `ElementDataSourceGate` composes, without converting it twice": green;
- `RecordRelatedListRenderer.elementDataSource.test.tsx` "hands the composed view-AND-binding filter to the list (objectstack#7118)": green;
- `@object-ui/plugin-detail` `type-check`: green. It compiles the typed hand-off `filter={schema.filter}` into the union prop.

## Ablation (restore `any`): the pin goes red

This was run with `node ../objectstack/scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode on committed HEAD `76fe2952`. Anchor `  filter?: ViewFilterRule[];` hit once, and the replacement was `  filter?: any;`. On disk the anchor went 1 → 0 and the replacement 0 → 1 (also counted by `grep -c` inside the wrapped command: `anchor=0 any=1`). The blob went `99358850ceb9` → `90d7de2c30af`.

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` → exit 2, from 5 errors, all in the pin. There were 2 × `TS2344` (the two `Equal` legs) and **3 × `TS2578` unused `@ts-expect-error`**: `_AnyIsNotTheContract`, the composed-node literal and the tuple-array literal.
- `vitest run` on the pin → **10 failed / 5 passed**. The seven flip cases, the agreement leg and both discrimination legs went red. The canonical case and the three controls stayed green, as they should.
- Restore: the blob after restore was `99358850ceb9`, equal to the HEAD blob, and `git diff HEAD` came back empty (the tool's own proof, re-read independently afterwards).

No build sits in this ablation's path: the pin reads `../record-components` by relative path, and `tsconfig.test.json` clears `paths`, so only `@objectstack/spec` resolves through node_modules.

## Changeset level: `minor`, with the break spelled out

This narrows a published type. A TypeScript author who annotated a value with `RecordRelatedListComponentProps` and assigned a non-array `filter` stops compiling. This repo declares its own breaks as `minor` (AGENTS.md version alignment: the fixed group's major follows `@objectstack`, and `check-changeset-no-major` enforces it). The body names each refused shape and gives a one-line migration: "author the rule array, `[{ field, operator, value }]`; the composed node is runtime-only." The protocol's parse already refuses every one of those shapes on this key, so no publishable metadata changes meaning, and nothing changes at runtime.

## Verification (at head `f42c7c7f`, after merging `origin/main` `1dbb9933`, which carries objectui#10315)

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` (main, examples and test tsconfigs): exit 0.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/types/` from the repo root: **215 files, 4938 tests passed**.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail type-check` (main and test): exit 0. This ran against the `@object-ui/types` dist built from this branch. `record-components.ts` is unchanged since that build, verified with `git diff --quiet`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/plugin-detail/` from the repo root: **199 passed, 1 skipped files; 2002 passed, 8 skipped tests**. It ran at `f42c7c7f` and earlier at `42097898`, with the same counts.
- Reverse probe that plugin-detail reads the rebuilt narrowed types rather than a cache: a throwaway test file, deleted afterwards with `git status` clean. Assigning an array of tuples to `RecordRelatedListComponentProps` and to the renderer's `schema` type gave `TS2322` twice. The renderer body's `schema.filter` reads exactly `ViewFilterRule[] | undefined`, and the rule array compiles.
- Lint: `eslint .` over `packages/types` (that package's own `lint` script, 286 files by the `--format json` count) gave 0 errors. The three changed `.ts` files are in that population. There are two `no-explicit-any` **warnings** in the new pin, both deliberate: `Equal` of `any` and `true` and the "is not `any`" assertion, the same shape as the 9964 pin. `lint.yml` sets no `--max-warnings`.
- Gates: `check:spec-symbols`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:test-path-roots` and `check-changeset-presence` (1 released package, 1 changeset) all passed. So did `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:changeset-claims` and `check-governed-queue-guard --test` over the four paths (NOT GOVERNED). `check:changeset-claims` found no self-contradiction. It asked me to re-read 4 pending changesets that name a file this diff edits (8604, 9040, 9187 for `p1-spec-alignment.test.ts`, and 9280 for `record-components.ts`). I read each paragraph, and each still holds, because this diff moves only the related-list `filter` in both files.
- `Spec Main Shape Gate`: this branch now contains objectui#10315, so the objectui#10287 red should not recur. CI's verdict is not read here.

## Acceptance notes (observations, not filed)

- **The fenced renderer's local type now reads the narrowed face.** `RecordRelatedListRendererProps['schema']` is derived from this interface, so inside `record-related-list.tsx` the key reads `ViewFilterRule[] | undefined`. At runtime, after `ElementDataSourceGate` has run, the value there can be the composed AST node. Today the body's only read forwards the value to `RelatedList`'s union, so nothing mishandles it. A future read in that body that trusts the local type (for example, mapping over the value as rules) would be wrong under a binding. The ruling chose this split; it is noted for whoever next edits that file (objectui#10303 is in flight there).
- **A third runtime shape reaches the same key.** The FK field's `relatedListFilter` (the spec's MongoDB-style `FilterCondition`) is forwarded onto the synthesized node's `filter` by `RecordDetailView` → `deriveRelatedLists` → `buildDefaultPageSchema` (objectui#4664, which the plugin-detail README documents as the third producer). It travels untyped, is not persisted (Studio's page-create seed calls the synthesizer without `related`), and the consumer's `toFilterNodeSafely` lowers it. Neither the narrowed face nor the consumer's declared union names this shape, and `RelatedList`'s prop doc says "Two shapes arrive". This is a type-honesty observation with no reachable failure.
- **`operator` is not checked on this face.** `ViewFilterRule` is the spec's `z.input`, and its `operator` goes through `z.preprocess`, so the TypeScript `operator` type is `unknown`. A misspelled operator therefore compiles, and the protocol's parse refuses it. This comes from the spec side and is out of this card's scope.
